findings.evidence: KV 24.1 GB per request (24.9 GB on the 9.5K-token slot-counting basis) against the 640 GB pool.
findings.issue: The sentence gives the two KV bases but does not state that the 640 GB pool must first subtract weights and the runtime reserve before it is a KV budget. A reader can misread 'against the 640 GB pool' as a fit check, while the chapter elsewhere correctly uses the ~436 GB KV budget.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the denominator clarification: 'against the 640 GB pool — i.e. the ~436 GB KV budget after weights and the ~64 GB reserve'.

findings.evidence: Table 2-2 row 'Prefill: regime verdict': "weight-only arithmetic intensity ~9.2K FLOP/byte — an upper bound that omits the ~24 GB KV write; including it, ~7,850 FLOP/byte (Ch 8) — both > ridge ~295 → on the compute-bound side of the roofline". Arithmetic: 1.29 PFLOP ÷ 140 GB = 9,214 FLOP/byte; 1.29 PFLOP ÷ (140 + 24.1) GB = 7,861 FLOP/byte ≈ 7,850.
findings.issue: The cell as written is internally ordered correctly (weight-only first, then 'including it'), but the sentence structure makes 'upper bound that omits…' modify 9.2K and 'including it' modify 7,850 — which is correct — yet 7,850 < 9,200, so 'including it' reduces the ratio. A reader skimming 'both > ridge 295' may conclude 7,850 > 9,200 or that including KV raises intensity. More importantly, the sentence 'including it, ~7,850 FLOP/byte' in isolation reads as if including the KV write gives 7,850 as an *increase* over 9.2K. The correct reading is that 7,850 is the *reduced* (still above-ridge) intensity once KV-write bytes are added to the denominator. This ordering error recurs in Fig. 2.2's caption on page 28 which says 'counting that write puts the same point at ~7,850 FLOP/byte — still well right of the ridge' (also correct but similarly ambiguous in direction).
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the cell as: 'weight-only arithmetic intensity = 1.29 PFLOP ÷ 140 GB ≈ 9,214 FLOP/byte (upper bound, omits KV write); adding the ~24 GB KV write to the denominator gives ≈ 7,861 FLOP/byte — lower but still ≫ ridge ~295.' Make the direction explicit: including KV write *lowers* intensity.

findings.page: PDF p. 45 (printed p. 21); PDF p. 72 (printed p. 48); PDF p. 119 footnote 3 (printed p. 95); PDF p. 130 footnote 4 (printed p. 106)
findings.evidence: Preface, PDF p. 21 (printed p. xvii): "the separately dated 2026-10-28 technology notes in the body and Appendix A carry revision v20260913+addendum-20261028". Ch. 2 §2.1.2 instead writes only: "Implementation note inspected on 28 October 2026, outside the 30 August 2026 evidence snapshot" and "[1P][FACT] (Wan2.2 sampling loop, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28.)". Ch. 3 §3.6.2: "(Wan2.2 source, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28)". Ch. 5 footnote 3: "retrieved 2026-10-28 (post-cutoff addendum: outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff; retained because these pinned first-party sources are the only verifiable record of the cited behavior)". Compare Ch. 7, PDF p. 160 (printed p. 136): "post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff".
findings.issue: Post-cutoff notes in Chs. 2, 3 and 5 do not carry the addendum revision identifier that the Preface assigns to the 2026-10-28 body notes; only Ch. 7's does. A reader (or the Sources chapter's edition-history panel) therefore cannot tell which 2026-10-28 notes belong to v20260913+addendum-20261028, and the Preface's claim that the body notes "carry revision v20260913+addendum-20261028" is not borne out by the body.
findings.fix_instruction: Append the revision string (v20260913+addendum-20261028) to every 2026-10-28 note in Chs. 2, 3 and 5, matching the Ch. 7 form, or amend the Preface to list exactly which notes carry it.

findings.evidence: "The short version, each mechanism bound to the one constraint it attacks: the KV cache itself is the capacity demand (it is the state, and its size per sequence is what must fit); PagedAttention → fragmentation (it manages where that state lives on the device and wastes less of it); prefix caching → redundant compute (it avoids computing a shared prefix's K/V twice); quantization → bytes per element (it shrinks each element); offloading → residency (it moves some of that state elsewhere)."
findings.issue: Ambiguous pronoun in a definition list: in three of the five parentheticals "it" can grammatically attach to the constraint on the left of the arrow, giving false readings ("redundant compute avoids computing...", "bytes per element shrinks each element", "residency moves some of that state elsewhere"). The list is the book's compact mechanism→constraint map and is reused in later chapters, so the referent must be unambiguous.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace "it" with the mechanism name in each parenthetical (e.g. "prefix caching avoids computing a shared prefix's K/V twice"), keeping one subject per definition.

findings.evidence: §2.8: "decode will be bandwidth-bound (a ~140 GB/token weight-read requiring ~5.6 TB/s sustained over each ~25 ms decode step (aggregate, hypothetical single-device figure; sharded across 8 GPUs it is 17.5 GB/GPU = 700 GB/s per GPU))"; §2.1 (p. 39): "why, at the canonical low-batch operating point, decode is HBM-bandwidth-bound"; vs Table 2-2 (p. 49): "weight-read bandwidth is not the binding constraint at this operating point" (700 GB/s of 3.35 TB/s per GPU, ~21%).
findings.issue: The chapter's summary surfaces restate the decode bottleneck using the hypothetical single-device 5.6 TB/s aggregate that Table 2-2 itself labels 'an aggregate figure, not a per-GPU one' and whose canonical-host verdict is 'bandwidth not binding at this point (weight-read only)'. The take-away an architect carries (size decode for 5.6 TB/s) contradicts the worked example the same chapter just derived.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite §2.8 (and qualify §2.1's question) to state the canonical verdict on the per-GPU shard figure (17.5 GB / 3.35 TB/s ≈ 5.2 ms, ~21% of the 25 ms step), reserving 'bandwidth-bound' for the intensity-based regime classification, with the 5.6 TB/s aggregate explicitly marked as the non-deployable single-device illustration.

findings.evidence: Convention (p. 23): "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." Violations: "Ch 4 §4.3 quotes this formula verbatim" (p. 40); "(Ch 3 §3.6, Ch 18)" (p. 74); "matching Ch 4 §4.6" (p. 133); "resident KV slots (Ch 4 §4.3, §4.6)" (p. 136); "(86 in-flight ÷ 17 slots = 5.06 → 6 hosts, Ch 4 §4.3)" (p. 147); "Ch 4 §4.7 tags the same quantity the same way" (p. 153); "(technical note below; Ch 4 §4.3)" (p. 177).
findings.issue: The book's own cross-reference convention prohibits repeating the chapter number after the chapter name, yet the prohibited 'Ch N §N.M' form appears at least seven times across five chapters, while the compliant forms ('Ch 8 §3', '§8.3.3') are also used — the reference apparatus is inconsistent with its own stated rule.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalize every 'Ch N §N.M' occurrence to either '§ N.M' or 'Ch N § M', and add the pattern to the build's lint checklist so future chapters conform.

findings.evidence: "actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [2°][HYPOTHESIS] — a rule of thumb, not measured here" vs the Axis-1 definition (p. 20): "[2°] — reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark".
findings.issue: The [2°] provenance tag asserts a reputable second-hand source, but the same sentence disclaims any source ('a rule of thumb, not measured here'); a rule of thumb has no survey, textbook, or benchmark behind it in this citation, so the provenance tag is unsupported.
findings.fix_instruction: Either cite the second-hand source that reports the 60–80% range (keeping [2°]) or drop the provenance tag and leave the unattached [HYPOTHESIS]/rule-of-thumb status explicit.
